title: Ada Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine
summary: Ada Lovelace published notes on Babbage's planned Analytical Engine, including Note G, a method for computing Bernoulli numbers on the machine. She is often called the first computer programmer, a label historians dispute.
why: An early written program and vision of what a general computing machine could do.

unsung.contribution: Her 1843 Note G set out a method for computing Bernoulli numbers on the Analytical Engine.
unsung.recognition: The notes lay largely unnoticed until republished in 1953; historians still debate how much credit she deserves.
